title: Development Subdistricts
source_file: Residential Zoning Districts.pdf
summary: Sets residential lot size, setbacks and height by density level (VL, L, M, H, VH); contextual setbacks and heights may be used, and Chapter 915 environmental rules add limits.
quote: Development Subdistricts establish regulations governing site development within residential zoning districts. ... New development shall be allowed to use Contextual Setbacks and Contextual Building Heights in accordance with the provisions of Section 925.06 and Section 925.07

title: Site Development Standards
source_file: Residential Zoning Districts.pdf
summary: Very Low-Density (VL): minimum lot 6,000 sf; 30 ft front, rear and street-side setbacks; interior sides 5 and 10 ft (R1A 5, RM 30); max 40 ft/3 stories.
quote: Minimum Lot Size 6,000 s.f. Minimum Front Setback R1D, R1A, R2 & R3 Subdistricts 30 ft. ... R1D, R2 & R3 Subdistricts 5 ft, on one side; 10 ft. on the other side ... 40 ft. (not to exceed 3 stories)

title: Site Development Standards
source_file: Residential Zoning Districts.pdf
summary: Low-Density (L): minimum lot 3,000 sf; front and rear 30 ft (RM 25 ft); street side 30 ft; interior sides 5 ft (RM 25 ft); max 40 ft/3 stories.
quote: Minimum Lot Size 3,000 s.f. Minimum Front Setback R1D, R1A, R2 & R3 Subdistricts 30 ft. RM Subdistrict 25 ft. ... RM Subdistrict 25 ft. Maximum Height R1D, R1A, R2 & R3 Subdistricts 40 ft. (not to exceed 3 stories)

title: Site Development Standards
source_file: Residential Zoning Districts.pdf
summary: Moderate-Density (M): minimum lot 2,400 sf; front, rear and street side 30 ft (RM 25); interior 5 ft (RM 10); max 40 ft/3 stories (RM 55 ft/4 stories).
quote: Minimum Lot Size 2,400 s.f. ... RM Subdistrict 10 ft. Maximum Height R1D, R1A, R2 & R3 Subdistricts 40 ft. (not to exceed 3 stories) RM Subdistrict 55 ft. (not to exceed 4 stories)

title: Site Development Standards
source_file: Residential Zoning Districts.pdf
summary: High-Density (H): minimum lot 1,200 sf; front, rear and street side 15 ft (RM 25 ft); interior 5 ft (RM 10 ft); max 40 ft/3 stories (RM 85 ft/9 stories).
quote: Minimum Lot Size 1,200 s.f. Minimum Front Setback R1D, R1A, R2 & R3 Subdistricts 15 ft. RM Subdistrict 25 ft. ... RM Subdistrict 85 ft. (not to exceed 9 stories)

title: Site Development Standards
source_file: Residential Zoning Districts.pdf
summary: Very-High Density (VH): no minimum lot size listed; front/street side 5 ft, rear 15 ft (RM 25 each); interior 5 ft (RM 10); max 40 ft/3 stories (RM 180 ft).
quote: Minimum Front Setback R1D, R1A, R2 & R3 Subdistricts 5 ft. RM Subdistrict 25 ft. Minimum Rear Setback R1D, R1A, R2 & R3 Subdistricts 15 ft. ... RM Subdistrict 180 ft.

title: Site Plan Review
source_file: Residential Zoning Districts.pdf
summary: In RM districts, a new multi-unit building with 4 or more units, or enlarging or exterior renovation of one, requires Site Plan Review under Section 922.04.
quote: The following shall require Site Plan Review and approval in accordance with the Site Plan Review procedures of Section 922.04: i. Any new construction of a multi-unit residence that includes four (4) or more units

title: Site Development Standards
source_file: Special Purpose Districts.pdf
summary: Hillside (H) lots need at least 3,200 sf, have no setbacks, max 40 ft/3 stories, may disturb at most 50% of lot area, and building permits get Site Plan Review.
quote: Minimum Lot Size 3,200 s.f. Minimum Front Setback none ... Maximum Height 40 ft. (not to exceed 3 stories) Maximum Area of Disturbance: 50% of total lot area

title: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district
source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: Any construction or development in the identified floodplain needs zoning approval from the Zoning Administrator and a Bureau of Building Inspection permit, and must meet this section's flood rules.
quote: any construction or development anywhere within the floodplain unless zoning approval has been obtained from the Zoning Administrator and a permit has been issued by the Bureau of Building Inspection

source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: In the floodway, no fill, new building or other encroachment is allowed unless engineering analysis shows no rise in base flood levels, and a DEP permit is required.
quote: no encroachments, including fill, new construction, substantial improvements, or other development shall be permitted unless it has been demonstrated through hydrologic and hydraulic analysis ... that the proposed encroachment would not result in any increase in flood levels

title: Elevation and Floodproofing Requirements
source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: In AE and A flood zones, new or substantially improved buildings must raise the lowest floor, including basement, to the regulatory flood elevation; non-residential buildings may be floodproofed instead.
quote: shall have the lowest floor (including basement) elevated up to, or above, the regulatory flood elevation, or be designed and constructed so that the space enclosed below the regulatory flood elevation: (i) Is floodproofed

title: Residential Structures
source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: New or substantially improved homes in AE and A flood zones must have the lowest floor, including any basement, at or above base flood elevation plus 1.5 ft.
quote: any new construction or substantial improvement shall have the lowest floor (including basement) elevated up to, or above, the regulatory flood elevation ... means the base flood elevation (BFE) ... plus a freeboard safety factor of one and one-half (1½) feet

source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: Hospitals, nursing homes and correctional facilities may not be started, built or expanded in an identified floodplain area unless the City issues a Special Permit.
quote: the following activities shall be prohibited within any Identified Floodplain Area unless a Special Permit has been issued by the City. ... (1) Hospitals. (2) Nursing homes ... (3) Correctional Facilities.

source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: In AE zones without a mapped floodway, no variance may be granted for work that, with other existing and expected development, would raise base flood elevation more than 1 ft.
quote: No variance shall be granted for any construction, development, use, or activity within any AE Area/District without floodway that would, together with all other existing and anticipated development, increase the BFE more than one (1) foot at any point.

title: UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District
source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: Over mapped undermined land, the underlying zoning still applies, but builders must investigate mine conditions and may face limits or special construction techniques to reduce subsidence risk.
quote: This objective is implemented by requiring investigation of subsurface conditions in undermined areas and by restricting development in such areas or by requiring the use of specialized construction techniques in mine hazard areas.

title: Mines Underlying Property
source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: Before a Certificate of Occupancy for new construction or an enlargement, the applicant must submit all available Pennsylvania DEP information on mines under the property or adjacent properties.
quote: No Certificate of Occupancy application shall be approved for a use involving new construction or enlargement of an existing structure ... until the applicant has submitted all information available from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection

title: Single-Unit Dwellings
source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: A single house, or similar-sized structure, on undermined land may be approved if the owner shows more than 100 ft of cover over the mine and no nearby subsidence.
quote: competent evidence is provided to the Zoning Administrator showing that the site has more than one hundred (100) feet of overburden above the mine and that there is no known history of subsidence incidents in the vicinity

title: Other Development Prohibited
source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: Sites with under 100 ft of cover or nearby subsidence, buildings larger or heavier than a typical house, and hazardous uses need a professional site investigation showing reasonable safety.
quote: no Certificate of Occupancy application shall be approved for zoning for construction on any site that has less than one hundred (100) feet of overburden ... for any structure that is larger or heavier than a typical single-unit dwelling

title: Review by Chief
source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: If the site investigation recommends special construction techniques, no building or land operations permit is issued until the Chief of Building Inspection approves the plans as safe.
quote: no building permit or land operations permit shall be issued until construction plans have been approved by the Chief of the Bureau of Building Inspection as safe for the site in question

title: Use Table
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: The Use Table shows, for each district, whether a use is allowed by right (P), by Administrator Exception (A), Special Exception (S), Conditional Use (C), or not at all (blank).
quote: Uses identified in a district column with a "P" are uses permitted By-Right ... with an "A" are Administrator Exceptions ... with an "S" are Special Exceptions ... with a "C" are Conditional Uses

title: Single-Unit Detached and Attached Residential
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: In the H district, houses must meet topography, soils, vegetation, access and water/sewer conditions, and clearing is capped at 10% of the lot or 2,400 sf, whichever is larger.
quote: Single-Unit Detached and Attached Residential uses shall be subject to the following conditions in the H District. ... In no case shall more than ten (10) percent, or two thousand four hundred (2,400) square feet, whichever is larger, be cleared.

title: Topography
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: In the H district, the house must sit on buildable land: a contiguous part of the lot whose existing slope is under 30%.
quote: Primary structure must be located on buildable land defined as a contiguous area of the lot less than thirty (30) percent in existing slope.

title: Soils
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: H-district sites must be investigated for soils; the Zoning Administrator may require a soils engineering report, for example for building on natural slopes over 20% or landslide-prone areas.
quote: A soils engineering report may be required at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator. ... Any development proposed on natural slopes greater than twenty (20) percent; c. Areas that are landslide-prone

title: Single-Unit Attached Residential
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: In R1D districts, attached single-unit homes are allowed by right on lots 35 ft wide or less; on wider lots they need a Special Exception under Section 922.07.
quote: For lots with Lot Widths of 35 feet or smaller, Single-Unit Attached Uses shall be permitted by right. ... For lots with Lot Widths larger than 35 feet, Single-Unit Attached Uses shall be permitted by the Special Exception Provisions

title: Accessory Dwelling Unit Overlay District
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Allows accessory dwelling units in the mapped ADU overlay, limited to one per lot, with the owner living on site and leases of at least 30 days.
quote: It is the intent of this Section to permit the construction and operation of Accessory Dwelling Units ... in certain districts. ... No Accessory Dwelling Unit may be leased for a period shorter than thirty (30) days

source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: An accessory dwelling unit is a home under 800 sf serving a building with one legal dwelling; it may be inside the main building, detached, or in an accessory structure.
quote: Accessory Dwelling Unit means a dwelling unit smaller than 800 square feet in area, which is accessory to a structure with a legally established single dwelling unit.

source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: An accessory dwelling unit may be no taller than two stories or 30 ft.
quote: Accessory Dwelling Unit shall not exceed two (2) stories, or thirty (30) feet in height;

title: Administrator Exceptions
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Lists approvals outside the Use Table granted as Administrator Exceptions under Section 922.08, including single-unit dwellings in undermined areas and the infill-housing parking exception.
quote: The following uses shall be allowed as Administrator Exceptions in accordance with the Review Procedures of Section 922.08. ... 1. Single-Unit Dwellings (Section 906.05.B.2) ... Exception to Off-Street Parking Requirements for Infill Housing (Section 914.11.B.4)

title: Undermined Area Overlay District
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: A single-unit dwelling in the Undermined Area Overlay (Section 906.05.B.2) is approved as an Administrator Exception.
quote: B. Undermined Area Overlay District. 1. Single-Unit Dwellings (Section 906.05.B.2)

title: Special Exceptions
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Lists approvals outside the Use Table granted as Special Exceptions under Section 922.07, such as certain height exceptions and exceptions to the off-street parking schedule.
quote: The following uses shall be allowed as Special Exceptions in accordance with the Review Procedures of Section 922.07. ... Exception to Off-Street Parking Schedule (Section 914.11.A.1)

title: Conditional Uses
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Lists approvals outside the Use Table that are Conditional Uses under Section 922.06, including certain development in the Flood Plain Overlay District.
quote: The following uses shall be allowed as Conditional Uses in accordance with the Review Procedures of Section 922.06. ... A. Flood Plain Overlay District.

title: Off-Street Parking Schedules
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Sets minimum and maximum off-street parking by use: 1 space per unit for most homes (0 for attached single-unit), up to 4 per unit for single-unit and 2 otherwise.
quote: Single-Unit, Detached 1 per unit 4 per unit Single-Unit Attached 0 per unit 4 per unit Two-Unit 1 per unit 2 per unit Three-Unit 1 per unit 2 per unit Multi-Unit 1 per unit 2 per unit

title: Schedule A
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Off-street parking must fall between Parking Schedule A's minimum and maximum for the use, unless an Alternative Access and Parking Plan is approved under Section 914.07.
quote: Off-street parking spaces shall be provided in accordance with the minimum and maximum standards included in Parking Schedule A. In lieu of complying ... an applicant may request approval of an Alternative Access and Parking Plan

title: Off-Street Parking Exemption/Reduction Areas
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: In mapped Parking Exempt Areas, minimum parking drops by a set share: 100% Downtown, UC-E and Uptown; 50% in UC-MU, R-MU and Riverfront; East Liberty and North Side exclude residential.
quote: shall be decreased as shown in the following table for uses located in districts designated on the Official Zoning Map as "Parking Exempt Areas." ... Downtown Any use 100 East Liberty Any use except residential 50

title: Exception to Off-Street Parking Requirements for Infill Housing
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: The Zoning Administrator may waive parking for a single-unit detached or two-unit home on a lot under 2,500 sf if parking can't fit within setbacks and street parking suffices.
quote: exception to the off-street parking requirements for Single-Unit Detached and Two-Unit residential uses ... The lot size is less than two thousand five hundred (2,500) square feet; (b) Off-street parking cannot be provided on-site without violation of the setback requirements

title: Environmental Standards
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Sets grading, cut-and-fill, retaining wall, slope replanting, tree survey and tree replacement rules; the grading rules apply to all slopes.
quote: The Grading, Cut, and Fill Standards of this Section Shall Apply to All Slopes. ... Retaining walls or gabions may be permitted to support steep slopes, but shall not exceed ten (10) feet in height.

source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Finished grades of 15% or less are encouraged; cut or fill slopes may not exceed 25% unless a geotechnical report certifies them and walls or terraces stabilize the slope.
quote: Finished grades of fifteen (15) percent or less are strongly encouraged. Cut or filled slopes shall not exceed twenty-five (25) percent unless: (1) The applicant submits a geotechnical investigation report that certifies the safety and suitability of such slopes

source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Retaining walls or gabions may be used to support steep slopes but may be no taller than 10 ft.
quote: Retaining walls or gabions may be permitted to support steep slopes, but shall not exceed ten (10) feet in height.

title: Slope Revegatation Standards
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Slopes over 15% exposed or created during development must be replanted: at least one canopy tree, two evergreens, two understory trees and five shrubs per 150 sf.
quote: any slope in excess of fifteen (15) percent grade exposed or created during development shall be landscaped or revegetated with trees and other plant material at the following minimum planting densities per one hundred fifty (150) square feet

title: Tree and Vegetative Surveys
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: A tree survey is required for development applications on sites larger than a quarter acre (10,890 sf).
quote: The Zoning Administrator shall require a tree survey for development applications on any site greater than one-quarter (¼) acre (ten thousand eight hundred ninety (10,890) square feet).

title: Building Height and Setback Standards
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Near R1D, R1A, R2, R3 or H lots, covered development needs larger setbacks (often 15 ft) and max 40 ft/3 stories within 50 ft, 50 ft/4 stories at 51-100 ft.
quote: shall be a minimum of fifteen (15) feet. ... shall not exceed forty (40) feet or three (3) stories in height when located within fifty (50) feet ... fifty (50) feet or four (4) stories

title: Lot Size
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: No permit or approval is issued for a lot below the district minimum, except lots reduced by public-purpose conveyances, small utility sites and certain single-unit dwellings.
quote: No building permit or development approval shall be issued for a lot that does not meet the minimum lot size requirements of this Code except in the following cases.

title: Single-Unit Dwelling Exemptions
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: One house may be built on a lot legally platted or recorded before the code, and other undersized recorded lots may get a single house by Administrator Exception.
quote: shall not be interpreted as prohibiting the construction of a single-unit residential dwelling unit on a lot that was legally platted or recorded prior to the adoption of this Code.

source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: A single house on a recorded lot smaller than the Chapter 903 or 905 minimum may be approved as an Administrator's Exception under Section 922.08.
quote: A single unit dwelling on a recorded zoning lot with a lot area less than otherwise required by the provisions of Chapter 903 or of Chapter 905, may be approved as an Administrator's Exception

title: Lot Width
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Lot width is the distance between side lot lines, measured parallel to the front lot line at the minimum front setback distance.
quote: The minimum lot width shall be measured between the side lot lines along a line that is parallel to the front lot line and located the minimum front setback distance from the front lot line.

title: Density
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Density is the number of dwelling units per gross acre: units divided by lot area in acres.
quote: Density refers to the number of dwelling units for each (gross) acre of land. Density shall be calculated by dividing the number of dwelling units by the lot area (in acres).

title: Setbacks
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Setbacks are open space between a building's furthest projection and the property line, open to the sky except listed features; contextual front, side and rear setbacks may be used.
quote: Setbacks refer to the required unoccupied open space between the furthermost projection of a structure and the property line of the lot on which the structure is located

title: Contextual Side Setbacks
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: A side setback may match the adjacent lot's existing setback but not below 3 ft; houses on lots under 60 ft wide may use reduced side yards of 3-5 ft.
quote: A Contextual Side Setback may fall at any point between the required side setback and the side setback that exists on a lot that is adjacent ... but shall be a minimum of three (3) feet.

title: Height
source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Height is measured from average finished grade at the front wall to the roof, with rules for counting stories, exempt rooftop features, and optional contextual height.
quote: building height refers to the vertical distance between the average finished grade along the wall facing the front street yard at the base of the building and: 1) the highest point of the coping of a flat roof

source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: Zoning map and text amendment procedure (rezonings); the ADU overlay in 912.08.C was adopted this way.
quote: Adoption of both a Preliminary and Permanent Accessory Dwelling Unit Overlay District shall be in accordance with the Zoning Map and Text Amendment Procedures of Section 922.05.

source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: The Conditional Use review procedures that uses marked C in the Use Table must pass; Section 911.02 describes these as review by City Council.
quote: E. Conditional Uses Requiring Review by the City Council. Uses identified in a district column with a "C" are Conditional Uses ... in accordance with the Conditional Use review procedures of Section 922.06.

source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: The Special Exception review procedures under which the Zoning Board of Adjustment reviews and approves uses marked S in the Use Table.
quote: Uses identified in a district column with an "S" are Special Exceptions ... only if reviewed and approved by the Zoning Board of Adjustment in accordance with the Special Exception review procedures of Section 922.07.

source_file: Use Regulations - Development Standards - Measurements and Definitions.pdf
summary: The Zoning Administrator Exception review procedures under which uses marked A in the Use Table are reviewed and approved.
quote: Uses identified in a district column with an "A" are Administrator Exceptions and shall be allowed the respective district only if reviewed and approved in accordance with the Zoning Administrator Exception review procedures of Section 922.08.

source_file: FP-O, Floodplain overlay district. - UM-O, Undermined Area Overlay District.pdf
summary: The procedures under which the Zoning Board of Adjustment considers variance requests; subsection 922.09.E lists considerations the Board weighs.
quote: Requests for variances shall be considered by the Zoning Board of Adjustment in accordance with the procedures contained in Section 922.09 ... in addition to the considerations of Section 922.09.E.
